note: Real GitHub Copilot for PRs review-thread payloads captured from phoenixvc/retort via gh api graphql. Copilot posts inline review-thread comments only — no admonition markers, no nits, no severity prefixes. The adapter maps every inline comment to `suggestion` (Copilot's baseline) and the review summary (state: COMMENTED with body, separate from the threads) to `info`. Status derivation includes a PR-state precedence: closed/merged PRs are `resolved` regardless of thread state. adapter-copilot.md severity heuristics and status mapping should reproduce the `expected` block for each scenario.

scenarios.name: security-concern-suggestion
scenarios.description: Copilot flags a path-traversal-flavoured finding on an open PR. Body has no admonition marker — just prose pointing out a subtle bypass. Per the SKILL.md rule, severity is `suggestion`, NOT `blocking` (Copilot does not emit explicit blocking markers). Comment posted ~4 minutes after the head commit, so status is `new_since_push`. This is the load-bearing severity test: a security-flavoured finding still maps to `suggestion`, because consumers must not infer `blocking` from heuristic content matching.

nodes.body: The "preserved" scaffold-once branch bypasses the path-traversal protection used for normal outputs. `normalizedRel` can contain `..` segments from `themeSpec.outputs`, and `resolve(tmpDir, normalizedRel)` could write outside `tmpDir` when an output is marked existing. Apply the same tmpDir containment check (and ideally also ensure `existingPath` stays within `projectRoot`) before copying.

scenarios.name: test-quality-suggestion
scenarios.description: Typical Copilot inline review comment on a merged PR — substantive critique of test determinism. No marker, plain prose. The PR is merged so status derives from PR-state (`resolved`) rather than thread-state (which is `isResolved: false`). Severity remains `suggestion` — the baseline Copilot output level.

nodes.body: The “warns and falls back to defaults on YAML parse error” case uses YAML that might still parse successfully depending on js-yaml behavior/version, which would make this test flaky and could unexpectedly set VALID_TEAM_IDS to ['a']. Use an unambiguously invalid YAML payload (or mock yaml.load to throw) so the test deterministically exercises the catch+fallback path, and then assert the warning behavior if that’s the intent.

scenarios.name: outdated-thread-merged-pr
scenarios.description: Copilot thread on a merged PR with `isOutdated: true`. The file was edited after Copilot flagged it, so GitHub marked the thread outdated. Even though thread-state suggests `outdated`, PR-state takes precedence — merged PR threads are `resolved` regardless of thread-level isOutdated/isResolved. `headRef` is `null` in the GraphQL response because the source branch was deleted on merge — `head_pushed_at` is therefore null and cannot be used for `new_since_push` derivation. `line` is also null because the file was edited past the flagged region. Severity stays `suggestion`.

nodes.body: `runInit` now checks a `globalThis.__RETORT_TEST_CLACK_PROMPTS__` hook to supply the clack module. This introduces a test-only global override into production runtime behavior and can make `runInit` sensitive to unrelated globals in the process. Prefer keeping the test seam contained to module mocking (e.g., mock `./_clack-prompts.mjs`) and/or gating this hook behind an explicit test-only condition (env var) so it cannot affect normal usage.
